shortQuestions: The narrator is a reporter (correspondent) travelling to the front during the war to report on it. Exhausted by the long journey, the snowstorm and the bitter cold, and because his truck was held up by a landslide, he decides to rest for a few hours at a roadside hut.

Cheng-yu is about ten or eleven years old. When asked why nobody is home, he answers that his father and mother are at work (his mother is at the depot/his father on the road), so he is alone at home.
His father works on the road gang as a demolition man, blasting rocks with explosives to keep the road through Lingkuan Gorge open; his mother works at the depot/warehouse.
His 'job' is to keep the stove burning and to watch the telephone (and wake his parents/answer calls) — his mother gave him this duty, and he takes it seriously.
He says he cannot go to sleep because it is his job to keep the fire going and watch the phone; his mother told him not to sleep, and if he slept he would not be doing his work.

In the final paragraph the narrator wakes up, sees the boy still awake and on duty, and sets out again. He realises that the road ahead is open because of the work of people like Cheng-yu's parents, and that a long, hard but hopeful journey — and his own duty — is waiting for him.
Cheng-yu is a responsible, brave, serious and mature child. He respects and obeys his parents, is proud of their work, and takes his small responsibility as seriously as an adult's job.

At first the narrator is tired, cold and gloomy, impatient at the delay. Meeting Cheng-yu changes his mood: the child's sense of duty and the hard work of the road builders fill him with warmth, hope and admiration, and he goes on his way inspired.

The story conveys that every job, however small, is important and should be done with dedication; that collective hard work builds a nation. It also values family responsibility, discipline, courage and the contribution of ordinary people.
activities: Sample story — Lingkuan Gorge: Beginning — During the war a reporter travelling to the front is stopped by a snowstorm and a landslide in the Lingkuan Gorge. Tired and cold, he goes to a small roadside hut to rest. Middle — Inside he finds a little boy, Cheng-yu, sitting alone by the stove. The boy explains that his father works on the road gang blasting rocks and his mother at the depot, and that his job is to keep the fire burning and watch the telephone. When the reporter tells him to sleep, he refuses because it is his duty. End — The reporter sleeps for a while and wakes to find the boy still awake. As dawn breaks and the road is cleared, he continues his journey, moved and inspired by the child's sense of responsibility.

Discussion guide: groups list daily responsibilities at home — helping parents, keeping the room clean, buying groceries, looking after younger siblings, studying regularly, saving electricity and water — and discuss why sharing responsibilities is important, linking it to Cheng-yu's example.
